units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
bitterly.
So this is the high-born social tone I've spoilt by my ignorant, uncultivated behavior! Makin love to a married woman!
units.name: MALONE

units.text: He comes angrily between Hector and Violet, and almost bawls into Hector's left ear.
You've picked up that habit of the British aristocracy, have you?
units.name: MALONE

units.text: That's all right. Don't you trouble yourself about that. I'll answer for the morality of what I'm doing.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: coming forward to Hector's right hand with flashing eyes.
Well said, Malone! You also see that mere marriage laws are not morality! I agree with you; but unfortunately Violet does not.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I take leave to doubt that, sir.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Turning on Violet.
Let me tell you, Mrs Robinson, or whatever your right name is, you had no right to send that letter to my son when you were the wife of another man.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: outraged.
This is the last straw. Dad: you have insulted my wife.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: YOUR wife!
units.name: MALONE

units.text: YOU the missing husband! Another moral impostor!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: He smites his brow, and collapses into Malone's chair.
You've married without my consent!
units.name: MALONE

units.text: You have deliberately humbugged us, sir!
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: Here: I have had just about enough of being badgered. Violet and I are married: that's the long and the short of it. Now what have you got to say--any of you?
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: I know what I've got to say. She's married a beggar.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: No; she's married a Worker
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: his American pronunciation imparts an overwhelming intensity to this simple and unpopular word.
I start to earn my own living this very afternoon.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: sneering angrily.
Yes: you're very plucky now, because you got your remittance from me yesterday or this morning, I reckon. Wait til it's spent. You won't be so full of cheek then.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: producing a letter from his pocketbook.
Here it is
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: thrusting it on his father.
Now you just take your remittance and yourself out of my life. I'm done with remittances; and I'm done with you. I don't sell the privilege of insulting my wife for a thousand dollars.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: deeply wounded and full of concern.
Hector: you don't know what poverty is.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: fervidly.
Well, I want to know what it is. I want'be a Man. Violet: you come along with me, to your own home: I'll see you through.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: jumping down from the garden to the lawn and running to Hector's left hand.
I hope you'll shake hands with me before you go, Hector. I admire and respect you more than I can say.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: He is affected almost to tears as they shake hands.
also almost in tears, but of vexation.
Oh don't be an idiot, Tavy. Hector's about as fit to become a workman as you are.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: rising from his chair on the other ride of Hector.
Never fear: there's no question of his becoming a navvy, Mrs Malone.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: To Hector.
There's really no difficulty about capital to start with. Treat me as a friend: draw on me.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: impulsively.
Or on me.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: with fierce jealousy.
Who wants your dirty money? Who should he draw on but his own father?
units.name: MALONE
